messages:
maria: Heads-up — I opened a refactor PR that splits the `networking` TF module into `networking-core` + `networking-aws`. surface-level changes only, but providers are being hoisted. Please review the impact on provider pins and the lockfile. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/3421
kevin: thanks — can you summarize the risk list? i skimmed and saw provider blocks moved to root module. wondering about registry mirrors and provider_version constraints.
jen: also need to check any modules that depended on module-level provider aliases (e.g., aws.external). moving providers up can break implicit aliasing.
maria: risk list I have so far:
- provider pins now live in root -> lockfile regen required across all envs
- some team modules expect `aws.account` alias, we should either keep aliases or map them explicitly in the call sites
- k8s secret path in `secrets_connector` changed (k8s_secret_path -> secret_path) — small rename but affects existing state outputs
- potential state mv for module.namespace changes if we change module addresses

kevin: for lockfile, recommended flow? i can run in staging.
maria: recommended: locally run `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64` from repo root after updating provider blocks, then push lockfile as part of the PR. For CI: ensure `TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` and `terraform init -reconfigure` step uses that lockfile. Example commands:```bash
git checkout pr/3421
tfenv install && terraform init -reconfigure
terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64 -upgrade
git add .terraform.lock.hcl && git commit -m "regen lockfile for provider hoist"
```
jen: question on state mv — if we keep the module addresses the same (we're splitting internals but keeping callsites), we shouldn't need state mv. are we renaming module blocks?
maria: callsites remain the same for most services, but a couple of internal infra stacks reference module `networking` directly (not via root) — i'm adding a compatibility wrapper module that forwards to `networking-core` with old outputs. it should avoid state mv.
sam: regarding secrets wiring, do we need a migration for the secret path rename? current plan was to change module output name which will break downstream referencing resources in state.
maria: good catch — plan: keep old output name as deprecated with a TODO, emit both `k8s_secret_path` and `secret_path` for one release. then remove deprecated in next minor.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: Staging plan for `infra/stacks/infra-core`: SUCCESS (no diffs that will destroy resources).
kevin: i'll run an end-to-end plan in staging and post results. if you can add the lockfile regen + compatibility wrapper to the PR, i'll give LGTM after a green plan.
maria: will do. also adding a small README in the module folder describing alias mapping and provider expectations.
jen: nit — add a CI guard that prevents PRs from removing `.terraform.lock.hcl` unless explicitly updating it. we had regressions before.
sam: agree, we should fail fast in CI on lockfile mismatch. i can add that quick.
kevin: if anyone hits provider verification weirdness locally, try `terraform init -upgrade` + remove `~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache` then re-run lock. i've seen cached plugins cause checksum mismatches.
maria: thanks all — I'll push changes in the next hour. tagging @kevin for staging plan run. :thumbsup:
